hook_text: This house can be rolled up and carried away on the back of an ox.
clip_script: The Richtersveld. A Nama family, descendants of the Khoikhoi, cares for goats and fat-tailed sheep. Next to the pen, a dome-shaped house of bent poles and reed mats. When the grass runs out, the mats are rolled up and loaded onto oxen. The Khoikhoi were herders: milk was their main food, and animals were their wealth. For hundreds of years, they shared the land with San hunters. They traded, worked together and married, but sometimes fought over water and grass.
visual_style: Whiteboard dome house of poles and mats building itself, then rolling up onto an ox, with sheep walking to fresh grass.
mood: Steady and proud, like a long journey with the herds.
pacing: Slow build of the house, quick pack-up, steady walk to new grazing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a table comparing the San and the Khoikhoi.
